newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujimori decides to go ahead with Asian tour.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori decides to go ahead with Asian tour.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori decided on Wednesday to go ahead with an 11-day Asian tour despite a killer earthquake back home.
Fujimori said the importance for Peru's economy of the trip to the four Asian nations meant he must go ahead with the official visits.
"Initially I had decided to cut short my visit but as this is an official visit I have decided I will not be able to return as I wanted," Fujimori told reporters.
The president had already left Peru when the quake struck on Tuesday and learned of the tragedy in mid-air while he was flying from Lima to Tokyo.
"I have given instructions to government authorities to take necessary and urgent measures for those who were caught in that disaster," Fujimori said.
"I send my condolences to the nation and have told authorities to reach out and give all aid necessary."
After Japan, which Fujimori leaves on Thursday, he visits the Philippines, Thailand and Malyasia, returning home on November 24.
The 7.3 Richter scale quake struck at noon local time on Tuesday (1700 GMT, Tuesday) with the epicentre about 65 miles (100 km) southeast of the town of Ica in southern Peru.
It killed at least seven people, injured more than 500 and left tens of thousands of people homeless.
Fujimori did not give casualty numbers or damage estimates, saying he was waiting for confirmation of details.
The president said he also hoped a report about 300 miners being trapped underground was a false alarm.
First reports said the 300 workers were trapped at the Huanca gold mine, 310 miles (500 km) south of Lima.
"Earlier we had reported 300 trapped but this now appears to have been one of the many false alarms of the day," said Jorge Rodriguez, a police doctor in the nearby Peruvian town of Ayacucho.
Fujimori said Japan had offered immediate assistance of tents and blankets which would reach Peru within 48 hours.
Within hours of his arrival In Japan, Fujimori and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto were in discussions about how Peru could join the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
Fujimori, who is of Japanese ancestry, is making his sixth visit to Japan since becoming president in July 1990.
